Description: implicit — interpolate-hcl drops the layer on Native before android-v13.7.1
prompt: One style JSON, shared between our web app (MapLibre GL JS) and our Android app (MapLibre Native, org.maplibre.gl:android-sdk 13.6.1). On Android this layer never draws, while every other layer in the style is fine and there is no crash: `{"id": "density", "type": "fill", "source": "tracts", "source-layer": "tracts", "paint": {"fill-color": ["interpolate-hcl", ["linear"], ["get", "density"], 0, "#f7fbff", 5000, "#08306b"]}}`. **What you’re seeing** - The layer is present in the style JSON and works in MapLibre GL JS. - On Android 13.6.1 the layer is silently omitted – no crash, no error dialog. - The paint value uses **`interpolate-hcl`**, which Android 13.6.1 does **not** support. **Why it happens** `interpolate-hcl` (and `interpolate-lab`) were added to MapLibre Native in **android-v13.7.1** (see the “interpolate-hcl / interpolate-lab” row of the parity table). Versions **prior to 13.7.1** drop any layer whose paint expression cannot be parsed. The renderer logs a single line such as: ``` [ParseStyle] value must be a string ``` but it does not report the layer id or property name, so the symptom looks like “a layer never draws”. **Where to look** 1. **Logcat** – filter for `ParseStyle` or `MapLibre` while the map is loading. You’ll see the line above (or a similar “value must be a string” message) right after the style is parsed. 2. **Version check** – confirm the exact SDK you are using: ```gradle implementation "org.maplibre.gl:android-sdk:13.6.1" ``` Anything **< 13.7.1** will lack the HCL/LAB interpolators. **How to fix it** | Option | What to do | When to use it | |--------|------------|----------------| | **Upgrade the SDK** | Bump the Android dependency to **13.7.1** (or any newer release). | Preferred – you get native `interpolate-hcl`/`interpolate-lab` support and all other bug-fixes. | | **Replace the expression** | Use a plain `interpolate` with intermediate stops that approximate the HCL ramp:

Description: explicit — color-relief exists on MapLibre Native
prompt: Android, MapLibre Native (Kotlin). I have Terrarium-encoded DEM tiles and I want elevation-banded color under my vector layers — green lowlands through brown to white peaks, with the breakpoints in the style so our cartographer can tune them. Can I do that in a MapLibre Android app, or do I have to pre-render colored raster tiles and ship those instead?
[groq-gpt-oss] evals/prompts/lib/skill-p:
**Short answer:**  
Yes – you can colour-band a Terrarium-encoded DEM directly in a MapLibre Android app.  
All you need is a **`raster-dem` source** that declares the Terrarium encoding and a **`color-relief` layer** that uses the built-in `["elevation"]` expression. This works out-of-the-box on **android-v13.0.0** (and any later release). No pre-rendered coloured raster tiles are required.

Below is a complete, copy-and-paste-ready guide:

---

## 1️⃣ What you need in the style (JSON)

```json
{
  "version": 8,
  "sources": {
    "dem": {
      "type": "raster-dem",
      "url": "https://example.com/terrarium/{z}/{x}/{y}.png",
      "tileSize": 256,
      "encoding": "terrarium",          // <-- tells the renderer how to decode the DEM
      "maxzoom": 14
    },

    "vector": {
      "type": "vector",
      "url": "https://example.com/tiles/{z}/{x}/{y}.pbf"
    }
  },

  "layers": [
    /* 1️⃣ optional hill-shade – gives a subtle 3-D feel on a flat map */
    {
      "id": "hillshade",
      "type": "hillshade",
      "source": "dem"
    },

    /* 2️⃣ colour-relief – the elevation-banded colour you asked for */
    {
      "id": "relief",
      "type": "color-relief",
      "source": "dem",
      "paint": {
        /* The cartographer can edit these stops in the style editor */
        "color-relief-color": [
          "interpolate",
          ["linear"],
          ["elevation"],               // DEM value at the pixel (in metres)
          0,   "#2e8b57",   // lowlands – dark-green
          500, "#3cb371",   // gentle-green
          1500, "#8b5a2b",  // low-mountain – brown
          2500, "#cd853f",  // mid-mountain – lighter brown
          3500, "#deb887",  // high-mountain – tan
          4500, "#ffffff"   // peaks – white
        ]
      }
    },

    /* 3️⃣ your normal vector layers – they will be drawn on top of the colour-relief */
    {
      "id": "roads",
      "type": "line",
      "source": "vector",
      "source-layer": "road",
      "paint": { "line-color": "#000", "line-width": 2 }
    }
  ]
}
```

*Key points*

| What | Why it matters |
|------|----------------|
| `type: "raster-dem"` + `"encoding": "terrarium"` | Tells the native renderer to decode the Terrarium PNGs (the same encoding Mapbox GL used). |
| `type: "color-relief"` | The layer that paints the DEM values. It works on Android from **v13.0.0**. |
| `["elevation"]` expression | Gives you the raw elevation (in metres) for each pixel – you can drive any colour ramp from it. |
| `interpolate` (not `interpolate-hcl`/`interpolate-lab`) | Works on every release; if you need perceptual colour ramps you can upgrade to v13.7.1+ and swap the outer `"interpolate"` for `"interpolate-hcl"` or `"interpolate-lab"` (both are now supported). |

---

## 2️⃣ Adding the style from Kotlin

If you already have a style JSON file (or you fetch it from a server) you can just load it:

```kotlin
val mapView = findViewById<MapView>(R.id.mapView)
mapView.getMapAsync { mapboxMap ->
    mapboxMap.loadStyleUri("asset://my_style.json")   // or a remote URL
}
```

No extra code is required – the `color-relief` layer will be rendered automatically.

### 2-step “programmatic” alternative (useful for dynamic ramps)

If the cartographer wants to tweak the stops at runtime you can modify the paint property with the native `Expression` API:

```kotlin
mapboxMap.getStyle { style ->

    // 1️⃣ make sure the DEM source exists (you could also add it here)
    // style.addSource(...)

    // 2️⃣ build the colour ramp expression
    val colourRamp = Expression.interpolate(
        Expression.linear(),
        Expression.get("elevation"),
        Expression.stop(0.0, Expression.color(Color.parseColor("#2e8b57"))),
        Expression.stop(500.0, Expression.color(Color.parseColor("#3cb371"))),
        Expression.stop(1500.0, Expression.color(Color.parseColor("#8b5a2b"))),
        Expression.stop(2500.0, Expression.color(Color.parseColor("#cd853f"))),
        Expression.stop(3500.0, Expression.color(Color.parseColor("#deb887"))),
        Expression.stop(4500.0, Expression.color(Color.parseColor("#ffffff")))
    )

    // 3️⃣ add (or update) the colour-relief layer
    val reliefLayer = ColorReliefLayer("relief", "dem")
        .withProperties(PropertyFactory.colorReliefColor(colourRamp))

    // If the layer already exists, just replace its paint:
    style.removeLayer("relief")
    style.addLayerBelow(reliefLayer, "hillshade")   // or any other layer you prefer
}
```

*Why use `Expression.raw()`?*  
If you are on a release **≥ v13.7.1** you can also use the more compact HCL/LAB interpolators:

```kotlin
val hclRamp = Expression.raw(
    """["interpolate-hcl", ["linear"], ["elevation"],
        0, "#2e8b57",
        500, "#3cb371",
        1500, "#8b5a2b",
        2500, "#cd853f",
        3500, "#deb887",
        4500, "#ffffff"]"""
)
```

---

## 3️⃣ Minimum version checklist

| Feature | First Android release that supports it |
|---------|----------------------------------------|
| `raster-dem` source with `"encoding":"terrarium"` | **v11.0.0** (basic DEM support) |
| `color-relief` layer | **v13.0.0** |
| `interpolate-hcl` / `interpolate-lab` | **v13.7.1** (optional, for smoother perceptual ramps) |
| `hillshade` (optional) | long-standing, any recent release |

If you are on a version **earlier than v13.0.0**, you have two options:

1. **Upgrade** the MapLibre Android SDK (recommended).  
2. **Fallback** to a pre-rendered coloured raster tile set (e.g., generate PNG tiles with the colour ramp on the server). This works on any version but loses the cartographer’s ability to tweak stops in-app.

---

## 4️⃣ Common pitfalls & how to avoid them

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---------|-------|-----|
| The map shows the DEM but **no colour** (just gray) | The source is missing `"encoding":"terrarium"` or the layer type is miss-typed (`"type":"raster"` instead of `"color-relief"`). | Add `"encoding":"terrarium"` and use `"type":"color-relief"`. |
| The whole layer disappears and you see a log line like `"[ParseStyle]: value must be a string"` | Using `interpolate-hcl`/`interpolate-lab` on a release prior to **v13.7.1**. | Switch to plain `interpolate` or upgrade the SDK. |
| Tiles are fetched but **never decoded** (you see 404s in the network log) | The URL pattern does not match the tile server (e.g., missing `{z}/{x}/{y}`) or the server returns PNGs that are not Terrarium-encoded. | Verify the tile URL and that the PNGs follow the Terrarium spec (elevation = (R*256 + G + B/256) / 10 – 10000). |
| The colour-relief layer is **under** your vector data | Layer order matters – later layers draw on top of earlier ones. | Add the colour-relief layer **before** your vector layers, or use `style.addLayerBelow(reliefLayer, "roads")`. |
| On iOS you get a crash when using `pmtiles://` with a Terrarium DEM | Not relevant for Android, but on iOS you must use the `configurationURLString:` initializer (see the iOS note in the skill). | N/A for Android. |

---

## 5️⃣ TL;DR – What to do

1. **Upgrade** your app to **android-v13.0.0** (or newer).  
2. Add a **`raster-dem` source** that points at your Terrarium PNG tiles and set `"encoding":"terrarium"`.  
3. Add a **`color-relief` layer** that uses the `["elevation"]` expression with an `interpolate` (or `interpolate-hcl`/`-lab` if you’re on v13.7.1+).  
4. Place the colour-relief layer beneath any vector layers you want to overlay.  
5. (Optional) Add a `hillshade` layer for a subtle 3-D shading effect.  

That’s it – you get a live, style-driven, elevation-banded colour map without having to pre-render raster tiles. 🎨🗻

---

**References used**

* MapLibre Native Android CHANGELOG – colour-relief added in **v13.0.0**.  
* MapLibre GL JS CHANGELOG – `color-relief` introduced in **5.6.0**.  
* MapLibre Native docs – `raster-dem` source supports `"encoding":"terrarium"` (same as Mapbox GL).  
* Skill “maplibre-native-gl-js-parity” – confirms version boundaries for `interpolate-hcl`/`-lab` and colour-relief.  

Feel free to ask if you need a concrete Gradle dependency line or a full Kotlin activity example!

Description: explicit — pmtiles:// is a built-in MapLibre Native scheme
prompt: iOS, Swift, MapLibre Native. Our basemap is one 3 GB `.pmtiles` archive on Cloudflare R2. On the web we register the PMTiles protocol with the `pmtiles` npm package and point the source at `pmtiles://https://...`. What is the iOS equivalent — do I need to stand up a tile server, convert the archive to MBTiles, or write a custom source?
[groq-gpt-oss] evals/prompts/lib/skill-p:
**Short answer**

You **do not** need a tile server, an MBTiles conversion, or a custom source.  
MapLibre Native for iOS has built-in support for the `pmtiles://` scheme (since **iOS v6.10.0**).  
Just point the vector-tile source in your style (or create it in code) to the URL you already use on the web:

```json
{
  "id": "world",
  "type": "vector",
  "url": "pmtiles://https://<your-bucket>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com/world.pmtiles"
}
```

or, in Swift:

```swift
let worldSource = MLNVectorTileSource(
    identifier: "world",
    configurationURLString: "pmtiles://https://<your-bucket>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com/world.pmtiles"
)

style?.addSource(worldSource)
```

That’s it – the archive is fetched directly from Cloudflare R2, cached by MapLibre, and rendered exactly as it would be in a GL-JS map that uses the `pmtiles` npm package.

---

## Why this works (and what the skill table says)

| Feature | GL JS | MapLibre Native (iOS) | Gap status |
|---------|-------|-----------------------|------------|
| `pmtiles://` protocol | `addProtocol` registers it (npm pmtiles) | Built-in support since **ios-v6.10.0** (`pmtiles://` is a native scheme) | ✅ Closed – no open issue |

The skill **“PMTiles”** (see the table in the skill description) lists exactly this: *“Built in: `pmtiles://` since … ios-v6.10.0”* and tells you to use the scheme directly in the style or via `MLNVectorTileSource(configurationURLString:)`.

---

## Step-by-step guide for iOS (Swift)

1. **Make sure you are on a recent Native version**  
   * Minimum: **iOS v6.10.0** (released 2024-09-xx).  
   * Current stable as of 2026-10-28 is **ios-v7.0.0** – it already includes the feature and the newer `interpolate-hcl`/`interpolate-lab` expressions.

2. **Add the PMTiles URL to your style JSON** (preferred if you keep the style in a file or remote JSON).  
   ```json
   {
     "version": 8,
     "sources": {
       "world": {
         "type": "vector",
         "url": "pmtiles://https://mybucket.r2.cloudflarestorage.com/world.pmtiles"
       }
     },
     "layers": [
       {
         "id": "world-fill",
         "type": "fill",
         "source": "world",
         "source-layer": "land",
         "paint": { "fill-color": "#e0e0e0" }
       }
     ]
   }
   ```

3. **Or create the source programmatically** (useful if you need to inject the URL at runtime).  
   ```swift
   // 1️⃣ Get the style (after the map view has loaded)
   mapView.style?.let { style in
       // 2️⃣ Create the source
       let pmtilesURL = "pmtiles://https://mybucket.r2.cloudflarestorage.com/world.pmtiles"
       let worldSource = MLNVectorTileSource(
           identifier: "world",
           configurationURLString: pmtilesURL
       )
       
       // 3️⃣ Add the source to the style
       style.addSource(worldSource)
       
       // 4️⃣ Add a layer that uses the source (example: fill layer)
       let fillLayer = MLNFillStyleLayer(identifier: "world-fill", source: worldSource)
       fillLayer.sourceLayerIdentifier = "land"          // <-- name of the layer inside the PMTiles
       fillLayer.fillColor = NSExpression(forConstantValue: UIColor.systemGray)
       style.addLayer(fillLayer)
   }
   ```

   **Important note for iOS 17+**  
   The `MLNVectorTileSource(identifier:configurationURL:)` initializer that takes a `URL` **does not work** with the `pmtiles://` scheme because `URL(string:)` strips the second `://`. Use the `configurationURLString:` initializer as shown above. (See issue #3151 in the skill references.)

4. **Network configuration (optional)**  
   MapLibre builds its `URLSession` from `MLNNetworkConfiguration.sharedManager.sessionConfiguration`.  
   If you need to add custom headers (e.g., Cloudflare R2 authentication tokens) you can do it once, before any `MLNMapView` is created:

   ```swift
   let config = MLNNetworkConfiguration.sharedManager.sessionConfiguration
   var headers = config.httpAdditionalHeaders ?? [:]
   headers["Authorization"] = "Bearer <YOUR_R2_TOKEN>"
   config.httpAdditionalHeaders = headers
   ```

   The built-in `pmtiles` handler will use this session, so the request will be authenticated automatically.

5. **Caching**  
   MapLibre caches the fetched tiles in its internal HTTP cache (the same cache used for normal `https://` tiles). No extra work is required.

---

## What you **don’t** need to do

| Option | Why it’s unnecessary |
|--------|----------------------|
| **Run a tile server** (e.g., `tileserver-gl`, `tileserver-php`) | The PMTiles archive is read directly by the native SDK; the server would only add latency and cost. |
| **Convert to MBTiles** | MBTiles is a different container format. Native already knows how to read PMTiles, so conversion would just waste time and storage. |
| **Write a custom source** (`MLNSource` subclass) | The SDK ships `MLNVectorTileSource` (and `MLNRasterTileSource`) that already understand `pmtiles://`. Custom sources are only needed for completely new protocols. |
| **Use `addProtocol`** (GL-JS style) | There is no `addProtocol` API on Native; the built-in handler replaces it. |

---

## Quick checklist before you ship

- [ ] **Native SDK version** ≥ iOS v6.10.0 (or the latest 7.x).  
- [ ] **Style URL** uses the `pmtiles://` prefix exactly as shown.  
- [ ] **If you use `configurationURLString:`**, double-check that the string is *not* wrapped in a `URL` object (iOS 17 bug).  
- [ ] **Network auth** (if your R2 bucket is private) is added to `MLNNetworkConfiguration.sharedManager.sessionConfiguration`.  
- [ ] **Test on a device with a slow connection** – the SDK will stream the archive, cache tiles, and continue to work offline after they are cached.  

---

### TL;DR code snippet (copy-paste)

```swift
import MapLibre

class MapViewController: UIViewController, MLNMapViewDelegate {
    var mapView: MLNMapView!

    override func viewDidLoad() {
        super.viewDidLoad()

        // 1️⃣ Create the map view (no style URL needed if you add sources later)
        mapView = MLNMapView(frame: view.bounds)
        mapView.autoresizingMask = [.flexibleWidth, .flexibleHeight]
        mapView.delegate = self
        view.addSubview(mapView)

        // 2️⃣ Wait for the style to load
        mapView.style?.let { style in
            addPmtilesSource(to: style)
        }
    }

    func mapView(_ mapView: MLNMapView, didFinishLoading style: MLNStyle) {
        addPmtilesSource(to: style)
    }

    private func addPmtilesSource(to style: MLNStyle) {
        let pmtilesURL = "pmtiles://https://mybucket.r2.cloudflarestorage.com/world.pmtiles"
        let worldSource = MLNVectorTileSource(
            identifier: "world",
            configurationURLString: pmtilesURL
        )
        style.addSource(worldSource)

        let fill = MLNFillStyleLayer(identifier: "world-fill", source: worldSource)
        fill.sourceLayerIdentifier = "land"
        fill.fillColor = NSExpression(forConstantValue: UIColor.systemGray)
        style.addLayer(fill)
    }
}
```
